To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a small number of anti-mouse-CD3 molecules are sufficient to stimulate a T lymphocyte, and that this number of anti- CD3 molecules can be found on the surface of cultured Langerhans' cells.
a small number of anti CD3 molecules on denditic cell accessory cells are sufficient to trigger T cells to enter the cell cycle.

(1) the number of anti CD3 molecules that are required to stimulate DNA synthesis is 200-300, (2) the FcR that are used for this presentation are not expressed by the T cells, and (3) the number of FcR per LC is decreased during maturation in culture
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which dendritic cells present antigens to T lymphocytes.
the role of FcR on dendritic cells in T cell activation, and the role of dendritic cells in antigen presentation to T cells.
the mechanisms of T cell triggering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of FcR on dendritic cells is small, and that this number is not increased by the presence of T cells, and that this small number is sufficient to induce DNA synthesis in resting T cells.
the LC is a very effective accessory cell in the polyclonal model of anti-CD-3 mAb, and that the FcR is the only molecule on the LC that can be identified as a ligand in the model system.
the number of molecules of anti-CD2 on dendritic cells that are necessary and sufficient to induce T cell proliferation is less than 1,000.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

dendritic cells can be "activated" to present antigens to T cells, but only when the accessory cell is sensitized to the antigen, and that this process may be independent of the MHC products that are required for antigen presentation.
dendritic cell maturation entails a series of changes in the cell that can be measured as the cell's ability to present antigen in the form of ligand to TCR.
LC can present antigen to T cells in a clonotypic manner, but that the presentation of anti-CD 3 is not a model for this function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of FcR on LC is low and that this number is not limiting for the response to anti-CD 3.
the number of ligand molecules required on dendritic cells to activate T cells is very low, i.e., in the hundreds.
dendritic cells may not need to present antigens in large amounts, but rather in small quantities.
